objective: Compile a 2D lattice world of autonomous settlements whose trade network self-organises from local surplus/deficit scans, and prove the result converges and stays connected.

equations.name: Cobb-Douglas production
equations.description: Output of resource r at settlement i. E is the territorial endowment (terrain yield x deposit richness), l the labour share with diminishing returns kappa=0.78, theta accumulated knowledge, R the road multiplier and sigma the shock modifier.

equations.name: Labour reallocation
equations.description: Decentralised adaptation: labour drifts toward the locally most valuable activity with inertia lambda=0.25 and sharpness nu=2.2. No settlement sees a price outside its own borders.

equations.name: Scarcity pricing
equations.description: Local price rises as the stock S falls below the target buffer S-bar = consumption x coverage_ticks. Elasticity eps=0.45, floor 0.25 and ceiling 6x the base price.

equations.name: Gravity attractiveness
equations.description: The trade-routing kernel. Masses are origin surplus and destination deficit, d the Euclidean separation with a d0=3 cell offset that keeps nearby pairs finite, c the terrain-weighted transport cost on the cheapest A* route, tau the freight friction and m the repeat-partner memory.

equations.name: Spatial arbitrage condition
equations.latex: p_j^r - p_i^r > \tau\, c_{ij} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad q_{ij}^r = \min\!\left(S_i^r, D_j^r\right)\eta \min(1, w_{ij}^r)
equations.description: A link only trades when the destination price premium covers freight. Volume is capped by the smaller of marketable surplus and unmet deficit, scaled by trade_fraction eta=0.45 and the edge weight.

equations.name: Edge weight dynamics
equations.description: Weights decay geometrically (delta=0.965/tick) and are refreshed by each discovery pass relative to the settlement's own best partner. Links whose weight falls below edge_min_weight or that stay idle too long are pruned.

equations.name: Logistic demography
equations.latex: \dot N_i = N_i\left[\rho\,\sigma(\text{food})\left(1 - \frac{N_i}{K_i}\right) - \delta_m\right],\quad K_i = K_0 + \kappa_E E_i^{\text{food}}(1+\theta_i) + \kappa_R R_i
equations.description: Population grows logistically toward a carrying capacity set by food endowment, knowledge and road access, gated by a food-security term derived from the granary buffer.

equations.name: Infrastructure feedback
equations.description: Sustained flow paves the route it uses: once cumulative volume on a link passes the threshold its whole cheapest path gains road level, lowering the cost c that feeds back into the gravity kernel.

equations.name: Ledger identity
equations.latex: S_{\text{end}} = S_{\text{start}} + Q - C + M_{\text{in}} - M_{\text{out}} - \Sigma
equations.description: Physical conservation across the whole lattice: production Q, consumption C, delivered imports, exports and spoilage must reconstruct the final stocks to floating-point tolerance. This is the mass-balance gate.

gates.description: population series must flatten: |exponential rate| of the final 25% <= 0.0045/tick
population choropleth must be spatially coherent, not per-cell noise
at least 85% of living settlements must sit in one trade component
the discovered market must carry at least one link per node
physical ledger identity must hold to floating-point tolerance
rendered frame must satisfy the visual specification
trade volume must recover to 60% of its pre-shock level
aggregate population must not collapse by more than 35% from its peak

economy.routing: gravity kernel over A* cheapest paths

risk_notes: The critical radius is a *geometric* lower bound: complementary endowments may sit farther apart than the lattice diameter suggests.
Ore is structurally scarce by design; if too few mining sites exist the ore price will pin at its ceiling and the corridor stays thin.
Spoilage keeps granaries finite; a settlement that cannot sell will still hoard up to its storage buffer.
